name: What Hidden Issues Show Up in Older Homes?

mainEntity.name: What hidden problems are most common in older Los Angeles homes during kitchen and bathroom renovations?
mainEntity.text: What hidden problems are most common in older Los Angeles homes during kitchen and bathroom renovations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes often look straightforward on the surface but reveal major issues once demolition starts. Kitchen and bathroom renovations frequently uncover deteriorated plumbing, electrical systems that do not meet current needs, water damage around sinks or tubs, framing that is out of level, and previous repairs that were not documented. These surprises can affect cabinet layout, tile work, ventilation, and waterproofing. That is why a pre-construction inspection and realistic contingency are so important. Homeowners should ask the contractor how hidden-condition discoveries are handled, whether demolition is phased, and whether subsurface or behind-wall work is included in the estimate. A careful renovation plan accounts for the age of the home rather than assuming the walls are clean and standard.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden problems include outdated plumbing, unsafe wiring, termite damage, water intrusion, mold, uneven framing, and past unpermitted changes. These issues are often uncovered after demolition begins and can affect both cost and schedule. Older homes should be inspected carefully before any finish selections are finalized.
